Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC:** Difficulty breathing after insect sting

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient was stung by an insect (bee vs wasp) on the arm a few minutes prior to consult.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Stung by insect (bee vs wasp) on arm a few minutes prior to consult

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Local reaction at sting site with slight redness, puncture mark, and blotchy rash.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Local reaction at sting site: slight redness, “hole”/puncture mark, blotchy rash

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports no notable swelling at sting site.
Patient reports difficulty breathing but is not acutely short of breath at time of call and is anxious it may worsen.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Reports “difficulty breathing” but not acutely SOB at time of call; anxious it may worsen

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports possible mild right lip swelling.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Reports possible mild R lip swelling

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports tongue feels a bit weird.

Past_Medical_History.content: History of occasional anxiety and panic attacks.

Medications.content: Patient is not currently taking any medications.
Medications.source_text: No meds taken yet; no antihistamines taken

Medications.content: Plan to start over-the-counter antihistamine: Chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg, 1 tablet up to 6 times per day, or a once-daily antihistamine per preference.
Medications.source_text:
Start OTC antihistamine:
  • Chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg: 1 tab up to 6x/day, **or** a once-daily antihistamine per preference

Family_History.content: Patient denies relevant family history of acute reactions.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works as a computer scientist.

Assessment.content: Localized reaction to insect sting (bee vs wasp) with mild erythema and rash at arm and no current evidence of anaphylaxis on video exam.
Assessment.source_text: 1. Localized reaction to insect sting (bee vs wasp) w/ mild erythema/rash at arm; no current evidence of anaphylaxis on video exam.

Assessment.content: Anxiety related to symptoms after sting.
Assessment.source_text: 2. Anxiety related to symptoms after sting.

Plan_of_Care.content: Start over-the-counter antihistamine for insect sting reaction and rash: Chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg, 1 tablet up to 6 times per day, or a once-daily antihistamine per preference.
Plan_of_Care.source_text:
Start OTC antihistamine:
  • Chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg: 1 tab up to 6x/day, **or** a once-daily antihistamine per preference

Plan_of_Care.content: Monitor for progression of symptoms and go to A&E urgently if lip or tongue swelling, worsening shortness of breath, stridor, or rapid deterioration occur.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Go to A&E urgently if lip/tongue swelling, worsening SOB, stridor, or rapid deterioration

Plan_of_Care.content: Seek review if arm redness spreads, feels hot, or there is concern for local infection as antibiotics may be needed.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Seek review if arm redness spreads, feels hot, or concern for local infection → may need abx

Plan_of_Care.content: No allergy testing indicated at this time; consider if recurrent similar reactions or non-specific rashes.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: No allergy testing indicated at this time; consider if recurrent similar reactions/non-specific rashes

Plan_of_Care.content: Provide patient information link regarding anaphylaxis warning signs.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Provide patient info link re: anaphylaxis warning signs

Plan_of_Care.content: Provide reassurance for anxiety and advise low threshold to contact service if worried or for symptom check-in.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Reassurance; low threshold to contact service if worried/for symptom check-in

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient should go to A&E urgently if lip or tongue swelling, worsening shortness of breath, stridor, or rapid deterioration occur.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Go to A&E urgently if lip/tongue swelling, worsening SOB, stridor, or rapid deterioration

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient should seek review if arm redness spreads, feels hot, or there is concern for local infection.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Seek review if arm redness spreads, feels hot, or concern for local infection → may need abx

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient advised to have a low threshold to contact the service if worried or for symptom check-in.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: low threshold to contact service if worried/for symptom check-in

Physical_Findings.content: On video assessment, breathing appears okay.
No visible lip swelling on video per clinician.
Physical_Findings.source_text: no visible lip swelling per clinician

Physical_Findings.content: Throat and oropharynx visualized with no swelling noted by clinician.
Physical_Findings.source_text: Throat/oropharynx visualized (asked to open mouth/say “ah”): no swelling noted by clinician

Physical_Findings.content: Arm and wrist sting site appears okay to clinician with no swelling seen.
Physical_Findings.source_text: Arm/wrist sting site visual inspection: “looks OK” to clinician; no swelling seen

Review_of_Systems.content: Patient reports possible mild right lip swelling.
Review_of_Systems.source_text: Reports possible mild R lip swelling

Review_of_Systems.content: Patient reports tongue feels a bit weird.
Patient denies notable swelling at sting site.
